name: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure BM.GPU4.8 / BM.GPU.A100-v2.8 / L40S
price_basis: per GPU per hour, as quoted by Oracle: BM.GPU.A100-v2.8 (8x A100 80GB) = $4.00; BM.GPU4.8 (8x A100 40GB) = $3.05; BM.GPU.L40S-NC.4 (4x L40S) = $3.50; BM.GPUA10.4 and VM.GPU.A10.1/.2 = $2.00; BM.GPU3.8 (8x V100 16GB) = $2.95; VM.GPU2.1 (P100) = $1.275. Published 2026-10-03.
notes: A100 80GB at $4.00/GPU-hour on OCI is genuinely competitive: it undercuts Azure ND A100 v4 on-demand ($4.10) and AWS p4de ($3.43 is close) and beats both on a bare-metal host with no vCPU/NRAM bundling. But the honest comparison is against the neoclouds, and there OCI loses badly - Runpod rents A100 80GB at $1.59 and Lambda at $2.79, both self-serve with no sales call. OCI's value is therefore not price per se, it is bare-metal NVIDIA with 8 GPUs in one host, which Runpod's and Lambda's single-GPU shapes do not give you. THE CRITICAL CAVEAT, repeated from the H100 record: availability is UNKNOWN. OCI's long-standing pattern of out-of-capacity errors on GPU shapes makes 'in-stock' a claim I cannot make from the price list, and this is the single most useful thing a reader could go verify with a real account. The A100 is a mature generation and is the shape most likely to have capacity if any OCI GPU shape does. Note the OCI-specific pricing convention that will trip up a comparison: Oracle bills OCpus not vCPUs, and a page-level OCPU rate is twice the vCPU rate because you get two vCPUs per OCPU - but the GPU figures are already per-GPU so that conversion does not apply to them.
